questions.question: Who succeeded Alivardi Khan as Nawab of Bengal?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Siraj-ud-Daulah **succeeded **Alivardi Khan **as the Nawab of Bengal after Alivardi Khan's death in **1756**. 
 
• He was **Alivardi Khan's grandson** and the **last independent Nawab of Bengal **before British rule. 
 
• Siraj-ud-Daulah is most noted for his role in the Battle of Plassey in 1757, where he faced the British East India Company.
 
• The defeat at Plassey, largely due to betrayal by his commander Mir Jafar, led to** British dominance in India**, marking a significant shift in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

• He toppled the Nasiri dynasty of Nawabs and assumed power himself.
 
• He is also known for his victory during the **Battle of Burdwan** against the Maratha Empire during the Maratha invasions of Bengal.​
 
 
 
• **Mir Jaffar & Mir Kasim**__
 
 
• British East India Company made** Mir Jafar** the first dependent Nawab of Bengal under them.
 
• **Mir Jafar was a successor of Siraj ud-Daulah** to whom he served as a Commander and betrayed him in the Battle of Plassey.
 
• **Mir Qasim** was the Nawab of Bengal from 1760 to 1763.
 
• He was installed as Nawab with the support of the British East India Company, **replacing Mir Jafar**, his father-in-law, who had himself been supported earlier by the East India Company after his role in winning the Battle of Plassey for the British.

questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for attending to disputes concerning recruitment and conditions of service of public personnel at the Centre?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Central Administrative Tribunal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Central Administrative Tribunal****​**

 
 
• The **Central Administrative Tribunal** was set on 1 November 1985 by the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.

 
 
• The Central Administrative Tribunal deals with service matters about the Central Government employees or of any Union Territory, or local or other government under the control of the Government of India, or of a corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government.
 
• The ​Central Administrative Tribunal consists of a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and members.
 
• Members are from both judicial as well as administrative streams.
 
• The **Central Administrative Tribunal** has 17 regular benches.
 
• 15 benches operate at the principal seats of High Courts and from the remaining two each one at Lucknow and Jaipur.
 
• These Benches also hold circuit sittings at other seats of the High Courts.
 
• Tribunal is a Quasi-judicial body.
 
 
• 
• Tribunals have the power to try cases of special matters which are conferred on them by statutes. The Tenure, terms, and conditions of the services of the members of the Administrative Tribunal are entirely in the hands of the Executive.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joint Administrative Tribunal**

 
 
• **​**​It means an Administrative Tribunal for two or more States established under the **Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.**
 
• A Joint Administrative Tribunal for two or more States shall exercise all the jurisdiction, powers and authority exercisable by the **Administrative Tribunals for such States.**
 
 
 
• **The Settlement and Appellate Tribunal**
 
 
• **​**The Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal established under section 14 of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 (24 of 1997), shall, on and from the commencement of Part XIV of Chapter VI of the Finance Act, 2017 (7 of 2017).
 
• Be the Appellate Tribunal for this Act and the said Appellate Tribunal shall exercise the jurisdiction, powers, and authority conferred on it by or under this Act.
 
• Under X chapter of the Information Technology Act, 2000 the provisions of the Appellate Tribunal are given.
 
 
 
• **The Competition Appellate Tribunal**
 
 
• The commission was established on 14 October 2003. It became fully functional in May 2009 with Dhanendra Kumar as its first chairman.
 
• Established by the Government of India under the Competition Act, 2002 for the administration, implementation, and enforcement of the Act.
 
• It is the chief national** competition** regulator in India.

questions.question: The drainage system formed when rivers discharge their waters from all directions in a lake or depression, as in the case of Loktak Lake in Manipur, is called ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **centripetal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Centripetal Drainage Pattern:**

__
 
• It is just the opposite of the radial as streams flow toward a central depression.
 
• During wetter portions of the year, these streams feed ephemeral lakes, which evaporate away during dry periods.
 
• Sometimes, salt flats are also created in these dry lake beds as salt dissolved in the lake water precipitates out of solution and is left behind when the water evaporates away.
 
• **E.g. Loktak lake in Manipur.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Radial Drainage Pattern:**

 
• The radial drainage pattern develops around a central elevated point and is common to conically shaped features such as volcanoes.
 
• When the rivers originate from a hill and flow in all directions, the drainage pattern is known as ‘radial’.
 
• E.g. The rivers originating from the** Amarkantak range; Narmada** and **Son (tributary of Ganga).**

**Trellis Drainage Pattern:**

 
• Trellis drainage develops in folded topography where hard and soft rocks exist parallel to each other.
 
• Down-turned folds called synclines form valleys in which reside the main channel of the stream.
 
• Such a pattern is formed when the primary tributaries of main rivers flow parallel to each other and secondary tributaries join them at right angles.
 
• **E.g. The rivers in the upper part of the Himalayan region; Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.**

**Dendritic Drainage Pattern:**

 
• It is the most common form and resembles the branching pattern of tree roots.
 
• The dendritic pattern develops where the river channel follows the slope of the terrain.
 
• The pattern develops in areas where the rock beneath the stream has no particular structure and can be eroded equally easily in all directions.
 
• Tributaries join larger streams at acute angles (less than 90°).
 
• **E.g. The rivers of the northern plains; Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.**

questions.question: The LCM of x² - 8x + 15 and x² - 5x + 6 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factorize both quadratic expressions by identifying the factors of the constant term that sum to the middle coefficient.

x² − 8x + 15 → Factors of 15 that sum to −8 are −3 and −5 → (x − 3)(x − 5)

x² − 5x + 6 → Factors of 6 that sum to −5 are −2 and −3 → (x − 3)(x − 2)

LCM is the product of all unique factors appearing in the expressions: (x − 3), (x − 5), and (x − 2).

**∴ The correct answer is (x − 5)(x − 2)(x − 3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expressions:

P(x) = x² − 8x + 15

Q(x) = x² − 5x + 6

To find the LCM, we first factorize each polynomial completely.

⇒ P(x) = x² − 5x − 3x + 15

⇒ P(x) = x(x − 5) − 3(x − 5) = (x − 5)(x − 3)

⇒ Q(x) = x² − 3x − 2x + 6

⇒ Q(x) = x(x − 3) − 2(x − 3) = (x − 3)(x − 2)

⇒ LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors present in the expressions.

⇒ LCM [P(x), Q(x)] = (x − 3)¹ × (x − 5)¹ × (x − 2)¹

⇒ LCM = (x − 5)(x − 2)(x − 3)

**∴ The correct answer is (x − 5)(x − 2)(x − 3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Polynomials

The Highest Common Factor (HCF) is the product of common factors with the lowest power. Here, the common factor is (x − 3), so HCF = (x − 3).

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two polynomials P(x) and Q(x), the relationship is: P(x) × Q(x) = HCF(P, Q) × LCM(P, Q).

Factoring Quadratic Trinomials

A quadratic trinomial x² + bx + c is factored into (x + p)(x + q) where p × q = c and p + q = b.</p

For any expression of the form **a sin θ + b cos θ = c**, the value of **b sin θ − a cos θ** is given by **√(a² + b² − c²)**.

⇒ x² = 2 − 11 / 9

⇒ x² = (18 − 11) / 9 = 7 / 9

• **'Major difference'** it emphasizes the significance of the two variation observed by the manager, indicating that it is substantial enough to warrant attention.
 
 
• **Example**- This is the third major difference between the two sets of meetings.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **'Major difference'.**
